title: Fiber Cement Board vs OSB: Which is Better for Facade Sheathing?
description: A technical comparison of fiber cement board and OSB for facade sheathing and exterior wall applications in European construction. CE certification, moisture resistance, fire performance.
author: Terasun Europe Technical Team
body:
## Fiber Cement Board vs OSB: Which is Better for Facade Sheathing?

When specifying sheathing for ventilated facade systems or exterior wall assemblies, European contractors and architects face a choice between several board types. Oriented strand board (OSB) and fiber cement board are two of the most commonly discussed options. This article provides a factual, technical comparison to help you choose the right product for your project.

---

### What is OSB?

Oriented Strand Board (OSB) is a wood-based panel product manufactured by compressing and bonding wood strands with resins. It is widely used in timber frame construction for wall and roof sheathing. OSB is available in several grades: OSB/2, OSB/3 (moisture-resistant), and OSB/4 (structural, high humidity).

**Typical properties of OSB/3:**
- Density: 600–680 kg/m³
- Weight: approx. 14–17 kg/m² at 22 mm
- Moisture resistance: classified for humid conditions, but not waterproof
- Reaction to fire: Class D (combustible)
- Swelling on wetting: 15–25% through-thickness (EN 317)
- CE marking: EN 300 (structural applications)

---

### What is Fiber Cement Board?

Fiber cement board (also called fibre cement board or FCB) is an inorganic building board manufactured from Portland cement, inorganic fillers, and reinforcing fibres. It does not contain wood or organic binders.

**Terasun TSM fiber cement board — key properties:**
- Density: approximately 1,020 kg/m² at 12 mm → **9.96 kg/m²** (lighter than OSB/3 at comparable strength)
- Moisture classification: **Category A** under EN 12467 — dimensionally stable when wet
- Reaction to fire: **Class A1** (non-combustible)
- Thickness swelling on wetting: <1% (test category A, EN 12467)
- CE marking: **1023-CPR-1565 P** under EN 12467
- European Technical Assessment: **ETA 24/0895**

---

### Head-to-Head Comparison

| Property | OSB/3 (22 mm) | Fiber Cement Board (12 mm) |
|---|---|---|
| Weight (kg/m²) | 14–17 | **9.96** |
| Fire class | D (combustible) | **A1 (non-combustible)** |
| Moisture behaviour | Swells 15–25% | **<1% swelling (Cat. A)** |
| Biological resistance | Susceptible to mould | **Inorganic — no mould risk** |
| CE standard | EN 300 | EN 12467 |
| European Technical Assessment | Not applicable | **ETA 24/0895** |
| Paintable | Yes | **Yes** |
| Suitable for exterior facades | Conditional | **Yes (all climates)** |
| Fire-rated wall assemblies | Limited | **E120 / EI90 / EW120 (tested)** |
| LEED/BREEAM documentation | Limited | **EPD-IES-0018268** |

---

### Moisture Performance

Moisture is one of the most significant differences between OSB and fiber cement board.

OSB/3 is classified for humid conditions, but it remains a wood-based product. In ventilated facade systems, OSB can be exposed to bulk water ingress during construction or through facade failures. Prolonged wetting causes swelling, edge delamination, and long-term structural weakening. OSB also provides a food source for mould growth if moisture levels remain elevated.

Fiber cement board under EN 12467 **Category A** is dimensionally stable when fully saturated with water. There is no organic content for mould to feed on. This makes it the preferred choice for:
- Ventilated facade systems in wet climates (Scandinavia, Atlantic coast, Alpine regions)
- Sheathing behind render (where bulk moisture is possible)
- Buildings in coastal or high-humidity environments

---

### Fire Performance

OSB is classified as **Class D** — it contributes to fire. This can be a limiting factor in multi-storey or public buildings where building regulations require limited combustibility.

Terasun TSM fiber cement board achieves **Class A1** — non-combustible, with limited smoke and no flaming droplets. The tested wall assembly achieves **E 120 / EI 90 / EW 120** (fire test report FIRES-CR-284-25-AUPE), enabling use in fire-rated partition and facade constructions.

For projects governed by Eurocode or national fire regulations requiring A1 or A2 materials on facades, fiber cement board is the correct choice.

---

### Weight and Structural Load

At 12 mm thickness, Terasun TSM weighs **9.96 kg/m²** — lighter than OSB/3 at comparable spans. This reduces structural load on fixing systems and substructures, which is particularly relevant in lightweight steel frame and timber frame constructions.

---

### When OSB is the Right Choice

OSB remains a cost-effective choice for:
- Internal sheathing behind a weathertight cladding layer in dry conditions
- Structural bracing panels in timber frame where fire class D is acceptable
- Roof decking under roofing membranes
- Projects where initial cost is the primary driver and fire class and moisture performance are not critical

---

### When Fiber Cement Board is the Right Choice

Fiber cement board is preferred for:
- **Ventilated facade systems** — all climates, especially Nordic and Atlantic regions
- **Fire-rated wall assemblies** — where E120/EI90/EW120 is specified
- **Render carrier boards** — as a substrate for mineral render systems
- **Wet rooms and bathrooms** — tile backing in fully wet areas
- **Steel frame construction** — non-combustible sheathing for lightweight steel
- **LEED, BREEAM, DGNB projects** — EPD documentation available (EPD-IES-0018268)
- **High-rise and public buildings** — where limited combustibility is required by regulations

---

### Summary

OSB and fiber cement board serve different purposes. OSB is a lower-cost structural panel suited for dry or protected conditions. Fiber cement board is an inorganic, non-combustible, moisture-resistant board suited for exterior facades, fire-rated systems, and wet areas — where OSB's combustibility and moisture sensitivity make it a risk.

For modern European construction — especially in ventilated facade systems, lightweight steel frame, and fire-rated assemblies — fiber cement board is the technically superior choice.

---

faq.q: Is fiber cement board better than OSB for facades?
faq.a: For ventilated facade systems, fiber cement board is technically superior: it is non-combustible (Class A1), dimensionally stable when wet (EN 12467 Category A), and resistant to mould. OSB is combustible (Class D) and can swell significantly when wet.

faq.q: Can OSB be used on exterior facades?
faq.a: OSB/3 has some moisture resistance but is not recommended for direct exterior exposure in ventilated facades, especially in wet climates. It swells and can delaminate over time when repeatedly wetted.

faq.q: How heavy is fiber cement board compared to OSB?
faq.a: Terasun TSM fiber cement board at 12 mm weighs 9.96 kg/m². OSB/3 at 22 mm typically weighs 14–17 kg/m². For comparable structural spans, fiber cement board can be lighter than OSB.
